label: AWS Cognito
note: Amazon Cognito user pools provide CIAM (sign-up, sign-in, MFA, token issuance). Guidance below applies to local user-pool users; federated users are secured by their upstream IdP.

questions.label: MFA methods
questions.text: Which MFA methods are enabled for user-pool sign-in, and is MFA required? (select all that apply)

guidance.text: **Strong posture.** WebAuthn passkeys are phishing-resistant. Ensure the user pool MFA setting is Required (not Optional), since optional MFA sees near-zero adoption.
**Good.** TOTP (authenticator app) is a solid second factor. Set MFA to Required for pools handling sensitive data, and consider adding WebAuthn passkeys for phishing resistance.
**Review.** SMS is exposed to SIM-swap and SMS-pumping/toll-fraud. Prefer TOTP or WebAuthn passkeys, and attach an AWS WAF web ACL to curb SMS abuse and bot traffic.
**Review.** Email OTP (Essentials/Plus tiers) is an acceptable baseline but not phishing-resistant. Add TOTP or WebAuthn passkeys for higher-assurance access.
**GAP.** MFA is off or optional. Set MFA to Required (set-user-pool-mfa-config with MFA ON) for pools handling sensitive data. Optional MFA results in near-zero adoption.

questions.label: Threat protection
questions.text: Is Cognito threat protection enabled (adaptive/risk-based auth plus compromised-credential detection), and in which mode?

guidance.text: **GAP.** Enable threat protection (Plus feature plan). It adds adaptive risk-based MFA and blocks sign-ins using credentials found in known breaches, both major account-takeover defenses.

**Review.** Audit-only logs risk but takes no action. AWS recommends a short tuning period, then switching to Full-function so compromised-credential and high-risk sign-ins are actually blocked or challenged.
**Good.** Full-function threat protection is active. Keep exporting threat logs to CloudWatch Logs / S3 / Firehose for monitoring, and provide user event feedback to tune risk scoring.

questions.label: Authentication flow
questions.text: Which primary authentication flow do the app clients use?

guidance.text: **Review.** USER_PASSWORD_AUTH sends the raw password to the Cognito API rather than using SRP. Switch app clients to ALLOW_USER_SRP_AUTH so passwords are not transmitted in the clear at the application layer.
**Good.** SRP or passwordless avoids transmitting raw passwords. Keep public client apps free of embedded credentials.

questions.label: App client credentials
questions.text: How are app client credentials handled for public (browser / mobile) clients?

options.label: Public client, no secret, PKCE enabled
Confidential client, secret kept server-side only
Client secret embedded in the app

guidance.text: **GAP.** Never embed a client secret in a public browser or mobile app; it cannot be kept confidential. Use a public client with PKCE, or keep the confidential client behind your backend. Do not place passwords, hashes, or AWS credentials in client-side storage.
**Good.** Public clients should use PKCE (OAuth authorization-code grant) and carry no secret. Generate a fresh code verifier per request.
**Good.** A confidential client is acceptable provided the secret stays server-side only.
